solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Discuss a letter about a cricketer

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the letter's spelt name wraps the sportsman

parts.note: the letter D is spelt out as DEE
a batsman is often called simply a bat

explanation.surface: Someone writes to the paper to argue over a particular cricket player.
explanation.walkthrough: The tempting reading takes 'a' as the letter A; instead the whole phrase 'a letter' is one spelt-out letter name.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss a question formally is to argue it out, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Puts down clerics without me

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the clergy surround the next word

parts.note: deans are senior clergymen
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the clergy have left them out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but in its older sense it means outside, the reverse of within.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to belittle or humiliate them, as does putting them down.

clue.text: Ban girl rendering Venetian boat song

parts.note: to bar is to ban or prohibit
Carole is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is forbidden from singing a gondolier's song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendering' looks like an anagram signal, but it only links the wordplay to the definition, in the sense of producing.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a song of the type sung by Venetian gondoliers, so the definition describes it directly.

clue.text: One who cares to make an offer

definitions.meaning: a nurse or carer, someone who looks after another, tends them
to put in a bid or formally offer, as in a contract

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person who tends something; the other is the verb meaning to submit a bid.

clue.text: Two cutlets at once

indicators.note: two signals that the same word is written twice over

parts.note: a chop is a cutlet of meat

explanation.surface: A diner orders a pair of cutlets served together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at once' looks like part of the order, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is an informal command meaning quickly, immediately.

clue.text: March increase

definitions.meaning: march here is a long walk, a trek
a rise, as in a price rise

explanation.definitionFit: A long tramp across country and a rise in prices are both called by the same short word.

clue.text: Don't cheat in two forms of leisure activity

parts.note: play is recreation, amusement
a fair is a funfair, a place of amusement

explanation.surface: A warning against cheating at games and amusements.
explanation.definitionFit: To act honestly and by the rules is the idiomatic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: A row between neighbours?

parts.note: row reads as a quarrel but means a line of bushes planted along a garden boundary

explanation.surface: Next-door residents falling out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' on the surface, a dispute; read it to rhyme with 'toe', a line of shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of shrubs separating two gardens is the classic garden boundary.

clue.text: Sack and what may be put in it

definitions.meaning: to sack a town is to pillage it

definitions.text: what may be put in it
definitions.meaning: loot or booty, which a robber might put into a sack

explanation.definitionFit: Pillaging a town and the booty seized from it share one word, and booty is carried away in a sack.

clue.text: Member of the forces — one holed up in battleground

indicators.note: holed up in means hiding inside, so the numeral goes within the battle site

parts.note: the Marne is a French river, scene of two great First World War battles
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soldier takes cover on a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine is a soldier serving with the navy, so a member of the armed forces.

clue.text: Arm on the leg

parts.note: arm reads as a limb but means a weapon, here a small dagger tucked into the sock of Highland dress

explanation.surface: A strange anatomy with an arm attached to a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: A SKEAN-DHU is the small knife worn in the top of the stocking with a Scottish kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon carried at the leg describes the small Highland knife kept in the hose.

clue.text: Tallest point in the High Street

indicators.note: in signals that the compass point goes inside the street name

parts.note: a town's High Street is abbreviated to High St on signs and addresses
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone names the loftiest spot in a town's main street.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual abbreviation of High Street, the main shopping street of a British town, takes the compass point inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of high means the same as tallest.

clue.text: A chartered accountant meant to return to scholastic life

indicators.note: to return means to come back, so the synonym for meant is read backwards

parts.note: aimed, as in intended

explanation.surface: An accountant intends to go back to university life.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic world of universities and scholarship is called by this term.

clue.text: Annoy by no longer working to a finish

parts.note: a machine switched off is no longer working
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Someone irritates by retiring at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend someone is to upset or irritate them.

clue.text: Strongly disapproves of what a model does after work

indicators.note: after places the model's action after the work in this down entry

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a model poses

explanation.surface: Someone objects to what an artist's model does once the work is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose something is to resist or object to it.

clue.text: Betray mum and ring head of police

parts.note: mum is a call for silence, as is sh
O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone informs on their mother by phoning the chief of police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not a mother but 'keep quiet', SH.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police.

clue.text: Robber holds up store

parts.note: holds up reads as an armed raid but literally means lifts, and the store is a shop, so this thief lifts goods from shops

explanation.surface: An armed robbery at a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A hold-up is armed robbery, but holding something up is lifting it: the thief lifts from a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who steals goods from shops is a store lifter.

clue.text: Two prizes lifted by the highest class

indicators.note: lifted in a down entry means raised, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a reward is a prize
a pot is a prize, as in a trophy cup

explanation.surface: Two trophies are raised by top-class winners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns REWARDPOT round to read TOPDRAWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for the best or highest social class.

clue.text: 17th century girl astride a horse

indicators.note: astride means straddling, so the girl's name goes either side

parts.note: Jean is a girl's name
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A girl sits on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astride' puts the horse, with its article, between the two halves of the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacobean describes the reign of James I, early 17th century England.

clue.text: Singular performance lacks dialogue

parts.note: singular here means by one person alone, so there is nobody to converse with

explanation.surface: A critic complains that an odd show has no conversation in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' looks like 'remarkable', but it means performed by one person.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo show has one performer, so there is no second voice for dialogue.

clue.text: Manage to define the bishop's position

definitions.meaning: a bishop is over his see, the diocese he presides above

explanation.walkthrough: A bishop's SEE is his diocese; he is set OVER it, and the two words make the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise work is to manage it, while the phrase also places a bishop above his diocese.

clue.text: Backs plans for junk mail

indicators.note: backs signals reading a word from back to front

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Someone supports schemes for sending unsolicited post.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwanted bulk email is known by this name.

clue.text: Fine food with party thrown in for a star

indicators.note: thrown in means put inside, so the party goes into the food

parts.note: manna, the food from heaven
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Lavish food and a party are laid on for a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna is a famous pop star, an example of a star.

clue.text: One must support the law to some degree in African state

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath, so the numeral comes below

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Each person must uphold the law, more or less, in an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some degree' looks like 'partly', but 'some degree' is the MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a country in south-east Africa.

clue.text: All together, Ben made a mess of back pass

indicators.note: made a mess of signals that these letters are jumbled
back signals that the following word is read in reverse

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Ben bungles a backward pass during a team game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a mess of' turns BEN into ENB; 'back' turns COL into LOC.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc is French for as one unit, all together.

clue.text: Sword play by Ibsen

definitions.meaning: a poetic word for a sword
An 1865 verse drama by Henrik Ibsen

explanation.definitionFit: An old literary word for a blade and the title of a Norwegian verse drama coincide.

clue.text: Excluded lawyers right to be in action

indicators.note: to be in means to sit inside, so the lawyers and right go into the action

parts.note: a deed is an action
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: Lawyers are banned from a legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: To be debarred is to be excluded or prohibited.

clue.text: Old invader of England involved in sacking

definitions.meaning: one of the Germanic people who settled Kent in the 5th century
a coarse plant fibre woven into sackcloth

explanation.definitionFit: One of the ancient Germanic settlers of England and the fibre used to make sacks share a name.

clue.text: Second murder results in police surveillance

parts.note: to take out is slang for to kill

explanation.surface: A second killing leads to the police watching a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A stakeout is a period of covert police observation.

clue.text: Draw in new capital

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: An instruction to pull in fresh money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money; it is the city, capital of Australia's Northern Territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwin is the capital city of Australia's Northern Territory.

clue.text: Risk death with passion

parts.note: death is the end
anger is a passion, a strong emotion

explanation.surface: A passionate person courts death.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to put it at risk.

clue.text: International codeword is rare in operation

indicators.note: in operation suggests these letters are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: A secret code is seldom used in a military mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Sierra stands for S in the international radio alphabet.
